subject: Order Form: fee-multiple structuring and exposure horizon proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@emergenthealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procure@emergenthealth.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed redlines to MSA / order form (liability cap)

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal went through the MSA redlines and attached our annotated version (Emergent_Redlines_MSA_20280613.pdf). Two points surfaced that I want to highlight so we can align quickly:

1) Liability cap basis: we proposed a cap equal to the greater of $1M or fees paid in the prior 12 months. Our intent is to ensure meaningful coverage for an annual production deployment while keeping it proportional to spend.

2) Annualization vs. aggregate: we prefer an aggregate (contract-term) cap rather than an annual reset — Emergent’s procurement says otherwise we end up underinsured for long-running projects.

We also flagged carve-outs for wilful misconduct, breaches of confidentiality, and regulatory fines (we flagged these as exceptions to the cap).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to the fees-paid 12-month basis or whether you need to anchor to total contract fees / a multiple of fees?

Attachments: Emergent_Redlines_MSA_20280613.pdf (redline)

Best,
Sarah Park
Head of Procurement
Emergent Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@emergenthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA / order form (liability cap)

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the attachment. Looping in Legal (Marissa, Laura) and our procurement lead (Karthik) to discuss options. High-level comments from our side:

- Fees-basis makes sense conceptually; we usually prefer an annualized cap (fees in the prior 12 months) because it limits long-tail exposure on multi-year contracts.
- As a counter-proposal we commonly offer: the greater of $500k or 2x fees paid in the preceding 12 months (annualized). For very large enterprise deals we will consider total-contract multiples (e.g., 3x aggregate) but only if there are guaranteed spend tiers.
- Carve-outs: we typically accept exceptions for gross negligence and will negotiate limited carveouts for IP infringement and confidentiality. We are hesitant to agree to unlimited carveouts for security incidents — instead we propose a separate security remediation bucket (e.g., defined incident remediation credit capped at $X) plus injunctive relief.

Next steps: Marissa — can you draft a compact counter-redline we can send to Emergent that: (a) sets the cap on an annualized basis (option A: greater of $500k or 2x prior 12 months fees), (b) includes a carveout list but narrows the security carveout to remediation/forensic costs and regulatory fines-related conversation, and (c) preserves exclusion of consequential damages?

Sarah — can you share if Emergent has a target cap multiple (e.g., they expect 1x, 2x) or whether they have internal procurement thresholds that force an aggregate cap? If you can confirm that, we can speed this up.

Thanks — I’ll wait for Marissa’s draft so we can send a short counter.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA / order form (liability cap)

Team —

See attached: Redwood_Counter_Redlines_20280614.docx and an Excel with fee scenarios (OrderForm_FeeScenarios_20280614.xlsx). Draft summary below for Hannah to share with Emergent:

Proposed counter (short):
- Liability cap: The parties agree that Redwood's aggregate liability for direct damages shall not exceed the greater of (a) $500,000 or (b) two (2) times Customer's fees actually paid to Redwood for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date the claim arises.
- Annualized vs. aggregate: This cap applies on an annualized rolling 12-month basis (to limit multi-year accumulation). If Emergent requires a single aggregate cap for the full initial term, propose a fallback: three (3) times the total fees paid during the initial 12-month period, with an explicit statement that renewal terms will re-evaluate cap basis.
- Carve-outs and exclusions: Exclusions to the cap limited to (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party IP infringement, and (iii) breaches of confidentiality causing direct regulatory liability. Security incidents: Redwood will not accept an unlimited security carveout — instead propose a security remediation carveout limited to documented forensic and regulatory notification costs not to exceed $2,000,000 in the aggregate unless there is a material finding of willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages: Standard mutual exclusion of consequential, incidental, and punitive damages remains in place except to the extent excluded by law or where damages fall under the limited carve-outs above.

Rationale (short): annualized caps keep exposure predictable and align with how we get paid; 2x provides meaningful protection for customers while avoiding outsized open-ended exposure. The security carveout cap is important for our carriers and budgeting.

Ask: Hannah — do you want me to send this as a tracked redline or a short bullet counter in a one-page note? I recommend the short bullet counter first to avoid line-by-line pushback.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@emergenthealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procure@emergenthealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines to MSA / order form (liability cap)

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Emergent's legal reviewed the bullets and prefers a one-page counter rather than tracked redlines — that should keep negotiations high level. Procurement confirmed they can live with an annualized basis if the multiple is 1.5x+; their internal target is 1x but they can stretch. Two asks from our side: (1) can Redwood move the minimum floor to $750k instead of $500k, and (2) can we see language that ties the security remediation bucket to a defined list of reimbursable cost types (forensic, notification, credit monitoring) so our security team can greenlight?

If you can send the one-page counter with the 2x/500k option and an optional variant (1.5x/750k) we can run both through procurement and come back quickly. Also please include a simple timeline for signature (we're looking at an early July go-live).

Link for DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/EMERG-RDW-1445

Best,
Sarah
